data.heroTitle: Sample three, park three, and give every parked concept a trigger
data.heroBody: The three durable-trend candidates that existing suppliers can make are worth $9.4K of the $24K budget. The three fads are parked with the evidence and a named condition that would re-open them — a parked concept with no trigger is a concept nobody will ever look at again.

sampled.name: Carbon steel wok 12"
sampled.rationale: Highest affinity in the set, best supplier fit, and the only concept that needs no tooling commitment. If one thing gets sampled this cycle it is this.
criteria: Hammering finish consistent across all three units in round one.
Seasoning takes evenly at 400°F with no warping on a home range.
Quoted unit cost holds at $19.40 at MOQ 500 after sample changes.
Handle weld passes a 40 lb static load with no deflection.

sampled.name: Whetstone angle guide
sampled.rationale: Cheapest and fastest concept on the list with the highest margin. Small ceiling at $34K a year, but it captures demand our own whetstone buyers are currently taking elsewhere.
criteria: Holds 15° and 20° within 0.5° across five units.
Fits our existing 1000/6000 stone without a shim.
Survives 200 sharpening passes with no visible wear.

sampled.name: Enamel roasting dish set
sampled.rationale: Strong durability read and Arcadia is our best supplier on every standard. The $4.2K mould deposit is the whole argument — it goes before the first sample exists.
criteria: Enamel matches the existing colourway within ΔE 2.0.
No chipping after 20 thermal cycles between 40°F and 500°F.
Nesting works in the existing carton footprint — no new box size.
Second RFQ confirms unit cost at $26.80 or better at MOQ 300.

parked.name: Countertop compost caddy
parked.why: Demand follows composting mandates rather than preference, has declined four quarters running, and concentrates in four states. Margin lands at 41% against a 42% floor before the $3.6K mould is amortised.
parked.trigger: Two further metro mandates take effect next spring. If either lands and search volume in those markets rises 25% over baseline, re-open with fresh economics.

parked.name: Magnetic knife rail 18"
parked.why: Peaked six quarters ago and has declined every quarter since. Good CM on a category we would be entering late, against entrenched review moats — and Kessler is mid-negotiation, which is not the month to add a tooling commitment.
parked.trigger: If any of the three incumbents delists, or category search returns to its peak quarter, re-open. Also re-open if we add a knife SKU that needs a storage attachment.

parked.name: Silicone lid-and-strainer combo
parked.why: Search spiked 141% in one quarter and has decayed for three. No existing supplier works silicone, projected CM is 38% against a 42% target, and two competitors who ranged it during the spike have already delisted.
parked.trigger: Only if we onboard a silicone supplier for another reason and the category is still measurable at that point. No scheduled check — this one is closed with its evidence attached.
